tone_statements.citation: Robert, Stéphane. 2024. Wolof: a grammatical sketch; and Lüpke, F. (ed.) The Oxford Guide to the Atlantic Languages of West Africa. Oxford: OUP.
tone_statements.quote: Wolof has a prosodic system typologically unusual in several respects. As most of the Atlantic languages, it is a non-tonal language, but in addition, it has no tonal accent and no pitch accent (Rialland and Robert, 2001). Wolof has fixed dynamic stress: the main stress falls on the first syllable of lexemes unless the second syllable is long, in which case it falls on the latter: 'daanu ‘to fall’, gin'naaw ‘back’, 'defaraat ‘to do again’. Moreover, the intonational system is remarkable because of the absence of any intonational marking of focus.
tone_statements.summary: Wolof described as non-tonal, with no tonal or pitch accent; fixed dynamic stress on the first syllable unless the second is long. Statement is for Wolof generally (Dakar variety), not Lebu specifically.

sources.citation: Voisin, Sylvie. 2023. Le wolof et ses variétés. La Linguistique 59(2): 69-99. doi:10.3917/ling.592.0069 (HAL hal-04278103, author version, 19 pp.)
sources.note: Nothing on word stress. Section 2.3.1 'Lebu' is historical/sociolinguistic; the article's data are morphosyntactic (noun classes, possession, conjugation). Useful as the survey of record: lists the Lebu descriptions (Diop 1994, 2001; Dramé 2012; Diagne 2015; Diouf 2016; Voisin & Dramé 2019; Voisin 2021) and notes Lebu is the most divergent Wolof variety, sometimes treated as a separate language.

sources.note: Nothing; TAM morphology across Wolof varieties incl. Lebu of Ouakam and Yéne (authors' own fieldwork). States (p. 330) that Dramé 2012 'propose une comparaison de la phonologie et d'une partie de la morphologie de trois variétés, le wolof du Saloum, le lébou de Ouakam et le wolof commun' and that Diop 2001 described the Lebu of Ouakam.

Contents = introduction, morphosyntactic particularities (demonstratives, possessives, pronouns, koon irrealis, incitative/negation), short lexicon, ~310 pp of interlinearised Petite-Côte Lebu texts (Yéen, Ndittax, Ngapparu, Géeréw, Rufisque, Kel/Tubaab-Jalaaw). tone.quote: Nous aborderons une étude contrastrive des deux parlers en examinant tour à tour la phonologie, la morphologie et la syntaxe. En phonologie, nous procéderons a un recensement des variations phonologiques aussi bien au niveau des consonnes qu'à celui des voyelles. Nous parlerons ensuite de la morphologie du nom et du verbe
tone.locator: Introduction, p. 15; Sommaire shows Part I Phonologie = I.1 Consonnes, I.1.6 Syllabe, I.2 Voyelles
tone.translation: We undertake a contrastive study of the two varieties, examining in turn phonology, morphology and syntax. In phonology we inventory the phonological variation in the consonants as well as in the vowels. We then discuss noun and verb morphology.
tone.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)
